patches.entity_key: Color adjectives from nouns are invariable
value: Colors that are true adjectives rather than nouns do agree (rose, mauve, pourpre, écarlate)

evidence.notes: Standard counterpart to the invariable noun-derived colors; medium confidence on the exact list for this textbook.

value: bon and mauvais use meilleur and pire instead of plus bon and plus mauvais
bien and mal use mieux and plus mal (or pis) as comparatives

evidence.notes: Standard irregular comparatives; the rule itself lists no exceptions, so these are supplied from French grammar.

value: With numbers, plus de is used without an article (plus de dix)
The comparison clause keeps que after the noun (plus de livres que de revues)

evidence.notes: First entry is standard usage; the second clarifies the stated word order, medium confidence.

value: Simple color adjectives used alone still agree (des robes vertes)

evidence.notes: The invariability applies only to compounds; the single-adjective agreement is standard grammar.

value: When a relative clause follows, celui qui or celui que is used instead of celui-ci or celui-là
-ci and -là attach to the pronoun itself, not to a following noun

evidence.notes: Both entries follow from the parallel demonstrative-pronoun rules; medium confidence on the first.

patches.entity_key: Conjugation of regular -er verbs in present tense
value: Verbs with spelling changes (manger, commencer, appeler, acheter) modify the stem
aller ends in -er but is irregular and does not follow this pattern

evidence.notes: Both entries are standard exceptions to regular -er conjugation.

patches.entity_key: Conjugation of verbs ending in -eindre and -aindre
value: The stem changes from -ein-/-ain- in the singular to -eign-/-aign- in the plural
The third-person singular form ends in -t (il peint), unlike regular -re verbs

evidence.notes: First entry is the rule's own formation; the -t form is standard for these verbs.

value: après que is followed by the indicative in careful usage
si is followed by the indicative, not the subjunctive
Conjunctions such as afin que, bien que, and pour que take the subjunctive instead

evidence.notes: First two entries come from the listed conjunctions; the subjunctive contrast is stated in the trap.

value: Conjunctions of cause and time such as parce que, pendant que, and puisque take the indicative
après que is followed by the indicative in careful usage

evidence.notes: Both entries come from the indicative list given in the companion rule.

value: With a dependent clause or infinitive, savoir must be used instead
The fixed expression connaître de nom takes de rather than a plain direct object

evidence.notes: First entry is the rule's own restriction and trap; the fixed expression is standard usage with medium confidence.
